section.title: Factor Perfect Square Trinomials
section.para: Some trinomials are perfect squares. They result from multiplying a binomial times itself.
The trinomial \(9x^2+24x+16\) is called a perfect square trinomial. It is the square of the binomial \(3x+4\).
If you recognize that the first and last terms are squares and the trinomial fits the perfect square trinomial pattern, you will save yourself a lot of work.
Here is the pattern: the reverse of the binomial squares pattern.

div.para:
If \(a\) and \(b\) are real numbers, then
\(a^2+2ab+b^2=(a+b)^2\)
\(a^2-2ab+b^2=(a-b)^2\)

section.para: Here is an example of how to factor a perfect square trinomial.
Step 1 - Does the trinomial fit the perfect square trinomials pattern, \(a^2+2ab+b^2\)?

list.item: Is the first term a perfect square? Write it as a square, \(a^2\).
Is the last term a perfect square? Write it as a square, \(b^2\).
Check the middle term. Is it \(2ab\)?

section.para:
Is \(9x^2\) a perfect square? Yes: write it as \((3x)^2\).
Is 4 a perfect square? Yes: write it as \((2)^2\).
Is \(12x\) twice the product of \(3x\) and 2? Does it match? Yes, so we have a perfect square trinomial.

Step 2 - Write the square of the binomial.
\(9x^2+12x+4\)
section.title: Try It: Factor Perfect Square Trinomials

problem.para: Write down your answer, then select the solution button to compare your work.

solution.para: Here is how to factor the perfect square trinomial:

Step 1 - Are the first and last terms perfect squares?
\((9y)^2\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;4^2\)
Is the middle term \(2ab\)?
\(2(9y)(4)=72y\)

Step 2 - Write the square of the binomial.
\((9y-4)^2\)

section.title: Check Your Understanding
section.div:
----------------------------------------
Which of the following is equivalent to \(36y^2+12y+1\)?
Correct! Check yourself: \((6y+1)^2=(6y+1)(6y+1)\), then, using the distributive property, becomes \(36y^2+6y+6y+1\), which becomes the given perfect square trinomial.
